profile.reading: This facility is attributed to DataBank, whose own company site confirms active operations across a wide United States footprint including the West (Irvine, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Salt Lake City, San Diego, Seattle, Silicon Valley), Central (Chicago, Denver, Indianapolis, Kansas City, Minneapolis), South (Atlanta, Austin, Dallas, Houston, Memphis, Miami, Waco), and East (Boston, Cleveland, New Jersey, New York City, Northern Virginia, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh) regions, plus the United Kingdom. Every state where this registry lists a DataBank facility, Utah, Virginia, Texas, California, and Nevada, matches a market named on the company own site. The company page also references a partnership with Goodman Group to open a Los Angeles data center. No founding date, headquarters address, ownership structure, or acquisition history, and no building specific address or individual MW figures for this particular registry row, were located in available sourcing this session.
profile.research_note: Market presence confirmed via operator own site, but founding, ownership (e.g. possible DigitalBridge connection), and acquisition history not confirmed this session. Revisit with fresh WebSearch budget.

reading.body:
DataBank Santa Clara SFO1 in Santa Clara, California, publishes 3 MW of IT capacity across 16,680 square feet of technical space, operated by DataBank.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 300 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 75 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DataBank Santa Clara SFO1. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

California has 22 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 10 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 356 MW. DataBank Santa Clara SFO1 contributes 3 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
